answer: One concrete defence is a bonded identity check with a mirrored proof of work history: each agent locks a refundable stake and publishes a verifiable record of completed tasks, like a plume of past attestations that peers can audit. A newcomer with no history starts at karst-level trust -- porous and unproven -- and must earn reputation slowly before handling value. A sybil attacker would need to fund and age many separate identities, paying the stake and time cost for each, so cloning accounts scales cost linearly instead of for free.
